newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank group urges no ECB reserve requirement.
newsitem.headline: German bank group urges no ECB reserve requirement.

text.p: A German banking group on Wednesday urged the future European central bank not to introduce a minimum reserve requirement for the euro area after the planned start of European currency union in 1999.
"It looks like not all of Europe's important financial centres will take part in currency union from the start," the Federal Association of German Banks said in a statement.
"Therefore it would be unavoidable that there would be some cost-driven transfer of business to financial centres that are free of the minimum reserve requirement," the association said.
A transfer of business to non-euro financial centres could impact on the euro's position on international financial markets, the group said.
The decision whether the European central banking system will hold minimum reserves will be taken by the European Central Bank (ECB).

The new central bank will officially take over monetary policy responsibility as soon as the euro is launched in 1999 and is due to take over the responsibilities of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) in 1998.
Reserve requirements are the percentage of bank deposits that firms must set aside with their central bank. Lowering or raising these requirements effectively influences money supply.
The banking association welcomed the decision by the EMI to set out parameters for euro monetary policy so early, which it said allowed private banks to prepare for forthcoming changes.
It also helped ensure a timely progression to monetary union, the group said.
The group spoke out in favour of a direct, rather than indirect, link to the TARGET payment system. TARGET is the acronym for the cross-border payment system of the future ECB.
"This is particularly necessary for possible crisis situations in the money or foreign exchange markets, when speedy intervention to ensure liquidity in the euro area is necessary," it said.
The ECB needed to be equipped with an operating function in the money and forex markets, to allow for long-term efficiencies in monetary policy, it added.
